What is the $y$-intercept of the parabola shown above?

**From top to bottom**, the **exact** values of the $y$-intercepts of the parabola shown above are{{field-1}}
and 
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(4,-3)$ and passes through the point $(-5,-6).$

The general standard equation of a left- or right-opening parabola with vertex at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(y-k)^{2}=4p(x-h),
$$

and substituting $(h,k)=(4,-3)$ into the above gives

$$
(y+3)^{2}=4p(x-4).
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(-5,-6),$ we substitute $x=-5$ and $y=-6$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(-6+3)^{2} & =4p(-5-4) \\ 9 & =4p(-9) \\ p & =-\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =-(x-4).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $y$-axis, we must have $x=0.$ So, we substitute $x=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =-(0-4) \\ (y+3)^{2} & =4 \\ y+3 & =\pm \sqrt{4} \\ y & =\pm 2-3 \\ y & =-5,-1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from top to bottom, the $y$-intercepts are $-1$ and  $-5.$
